title: PCEX missing-line program construction challenges
summary: Students complete a small program by selecting its masked line from one correct option and four or more distractors. The paper uses responses from 1,071 students to compare human-authored distractors with alternatives generated by five language models; students do not interact with the models during the challenge.

sources.title: Generating Effective Distractors for Introductory Programming Challenges: LLMs vs Humans
sources.evidence_quote: The student’s goal is to complete the program by selecting the missing line from a list of options consisting of one correct answer and four or more distractors.

assessment.summary: Choose the line of code that correctly completes a displayed solution to a short programming problem.
student_actions: Read a programming problem and an incomplete solution.
Select the missing code line from one correct option and several distractors.

student_role.description: Researchers generated candidate distractors with language models and evaluated them against historical student choices.

grading.method: The PCEX system records whether the selected option is the correct missing line.
